---
title: "Get started"
---

This guide walks an administrator through deploying Positron Server on JupyterHub.
Positron Server reads a license file that you place inside its own install
directory, and validates that file with the bundled `license-manager` binary.

::: callout-important
This guide covers Positron Server 2026.09.0 and newer, and 2026.06.1 and older.
Positron Server 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2 validate a signed token instead of a
license file, and need the extra setup on the
[verifier setup](verifier_get_started.qmd) page. See the
[version matrix](index.qmd#which-setup-applies-to-your-version) to confirm which
guide applies to the version you install.
:::

::: callout-note
To skip the steps on this page, the [deployment templates](deployment.qmd) page
covers a one-shot install script for The Littlest JupyterHub (TLJH) and a
docker-compose template.
:::

## What you need from Posit

Send email to [academic-licenses@posit.co](mailto:academic-licenses@posit.co) to
request a license file (`license.lic`). This file is proof of entitlement, and it
is the only file this setup needs from Posit.

Positron Server is free for educational use. For the eligibility terms, see the
[Positron Education License Rider](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/main/LICENSE.txt).

## Step 1: Install Positron Server in the single-user image {#install-positron-server}

Take the exact version string from the
[Positron releases page](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/releases), then
download and unpack the build for your architecture:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
POSITRON_VERSION=2026.09.0-256       # exact string from the releases page
POSITRON_ARCH=x64                    # x64 or arm64
CDN_ARCH=x86_64                      # x86_64 for x64, arm64 for arm64

curl -L "https://cdn.posit.co/positron/releases/server/${CDN_ARCH}/positron-server-linux-${POSITRON_ARCH}-${POSITRON_VERSION}.tar.gz" \
  -o /tmp/positron-server.tar.gz

mkdir -p /opt/positron-server
tar -xzf /tmp/positron-server.tar.gz -C /opt/positron-server --strip-components=1
```


::: callout-note
Positron spells the CPU architecture three ways. The download filename uses
`x64` or `arm64`, the Content Delivery Network (CDN) path uses `x86_64` or
`arm64`, and the activation directory uses `x86_64` or `aarch64`. Throughout
this guide, `<arch>` means the activation directory name.
:::


Place the license file next to the `license-manager` binary, in the activation
directory for your architecture:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
install -m 644 license.lic /opt/positron-server/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license.lic
```

::: callout-important
Mode `644` matters. Each single-user session runs `positron-server` as the
student, and `positron-server` reads and validates this file itself. A
root-only mode such as `600` makes every session fail to start.
:::

Confirm the license before you go further:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
/opt/positron-server/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license-manager status
```

## Step 2: Install jupyter-positron-server in the single-user image {#install-jupyter-positron-server}

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
# for example, in The Littlest JupyterHub
/opt/tljh/user/bin/pip install 'jupyter-positron-server>=0.0.5'
```

This proxy extension runs as the user. It adds the Positron tile to the
JupyterLab launcher and starts `positron-server` on the first request.

## Step 3: Point single-user servers at positron-server {#point-single-user-servers-at-positron-server}

Put `positron-server` on the session `PATH` by adding this to
`jupyterhub_config.py`:

```{.python filename="jupyterhub_config.py"}
import os

c.Spawner.environment = {
    "PATH": "/opt/positron-server/bin:" + os.environ.get("PATH", "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"),
}
```

This setup needs no license environment variables. Positron Server finds the
license file in its own install directory.

## Step 4: Restart JupyterHub {#restart-jupyterhub}

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
systemctl restart jupyterhub
```

Students can then select the Positron tile in the JupyterLab launcher.

## How it works

When a student opens Positron:

1. `jupyter-positron-server` kicks off starting Positron Server.
2. Positron Server validates the license file, and then starts.
3. `jupyter-positron-server` opens Positron Server with a connection token for the session.

```text
Single-user server
  jupyter-positron-server    starts positron-server on the first request
  positron-server            validates the license file and starts
  license.lic                mode 644, read by the session
```

A license file that is missing, expired, or altered stops the session from
starting. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd) for what each failure looks
like in the logs.

## Move an existing deployment off the verifier

If you set up Positron Server 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2 with the signing key
and the Hub verifier service, upgrading to 2026.09.0 or newer removes both. Make
these four changes:

1. Change the license file mode from `600` to `644`, so sessions can read it.
2. Remove `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` from `c.Spawner.environment`.
3. Remove the `positron-license` entry from `c.JupyterHub.services`, and the
   `positron-license-service` entry from `c.JupyterHub.load_roles`.
4. Delete the signing key at `/etc/positron/signing-key.pem`, and uninstall
   `jupyter-positron-verifier` from the Hub environment.
